text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's Foreign ministry said it had set up a new department which would be responsible for national security issues and the country's integration in NATO. @

-- Doctors and nurses from an emergency room in a hospital in Bulgaria's northeast Black Sea port of Varna issued an official statement demanding licences to carry firing arms to protect themselves against criminals who frequently came for medical aid after street clashes.
-- Bulgaria will face a shortage of a total of 1.07 million tonnes of fodder grain and milling wheat because of expected poor harvest this year, Agriculture minister Ventsislav Varbanov said. @

-- Ambassadors of the European Union member countries will visit Bulgaria's magnetic storage devices maker DZU in Stara Zagora on Tuesday to oversee implementation of measures against production of pirate CD's.

-- Bulgaria's Interior ministry said it had launched an investigation into the operations of the State Savings Bank (SSB) after SSB chairman Bistra Dimitrova said last week she was ready to submit her resignation to parliament.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided to raise the minimum pension by 12 percent from July in line with a rise in the average salary in the public sector in the first quarter.
-- Sofia and Belgrade restored the flights between the two cities following a lift by the United Nations three years ago of a 28-month ban on international flights for and from Yugoslavia.
-- Bulgaria's former interim Finance minister Svetoslav Gavriiski is likely to be the next governor of the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB), economic experts said.

-- "Strong-arm" insurance companies and criminal groupings are planning to obstruct the introduction of a fixed exchange rate system in Bulgaria by siphoning funds from state banks, Interior minister Bogomil Bonev said.
-- Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose by 62 billion levs in the first half of May to 392.3 billion levs, Finance ministry figures showed.
-- Bulgaria's Health ministry said it had set a five million lev tax to licence new domestic and imported drugs for local use. @

-- Bulgaria will sell locally ferrous and non-ferrous metals from its contingency reserves to obtain 60 billion levs for buying some 200,000 tonnes of wheat from the new crop to replenish state grain reserves, a senior government official said.
-- Austrian furniture producer Kaindl Kronopsan GR bought 51 percent of Bulgarian timber manifacturer Bules for $3.2 million, the Privatisation Agency said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
